# 09-karsa — sources

Back-test entry `09-karsa.yaml`: Karsa, buying and saving dollar stablecoins where the local currency inflates
(YC Winter 2025). Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's
choice" marks the smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Karsa (YC W25), 2025-01-30, 215 comments — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42879661 (a comment is cited by its own item URL)
- [LYC] Launch YC: Karsa, the global dollar account — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/MgV-karsa-the-global-dollar-account
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/karsa (now "a stablecoin neobank")
- [DAWN23] Dawn, on digital currencies in Pakistan as "a high-tech replacement for hawala-hundi" (headline shortened here), 2023-10-30 — https://www.dawn.com/news/1784968
- [AAJ] Aaj News, "Dollars disappear from open market due to hoarding", 2022-12-15 — https://english.aaj.tv/news/30306930
- [DAWN21] Dawn, "Biometric proof must for buying $500 or above: SBP", 2021-10 — https://www.dawn.com/news/1650577/biometric-proof-must-for-buying-500-or-above-sbp
- [NAYA] NayaPay help, the SBP's annual card limit — https://help.nayapay.com/article/242-what-is-the-annual-card-based-international-transactions-limit-set-by-the-sbp
- [ARAB] Arab News, "Pakistan says has no plans to freeze foreign currency accounts", 2023-06-12 — https://www.arabnews.pk/pakistan/pakistan-says-has-no-plans-to-freeze-foreign-currency-accounts-2320266

## Market

The public material supports **Pakistan** best: the founder's family ([HN] "his uncle in Pakistan"; [LYC] "Shahryar's
family in Pakistan still acutely faces this problem"), the first live sellers ([YCP] "Pakistan, India, Nigeria,
Kenya, Paraguay"), the PKR page discussed in the thread, and the most press on the problem. The segment and all twenty
respondents are in Pakistan. The eval's loader (`instructions/corpus.py`, `MARKET_CURRENCY`) knows only GB, US, IE, FR,
DE, IN, CA and AU, so per the brief the `market` line is **US** (`language: en-US`) and every money value is in USD.
Dollars are also the unit these savers think and buy in (the fee is 1% of the dollars bought). keel-cloud's own
`Market` table does not know PK either, though `Market.chosen` would take PK with an explicit currency.

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** People in Pakistan who earn in rupees and save.
   [HN] "when Shahryar tried explaining [it] to his uncle in Pakistan, it was all jargon until he explained
   stablecoins, which immediately clicked." → `roles[saver]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`.

2. **What (the job).** Keep savings from losing value.
   [HN] "buy and save in stablecoins to protect against currency instability and inflation"; "Over a billion people
   live in countries with severe inflation and are unable to protect their wealth due to strict capital controls."
   → `context.job`, `statements.problem`.

3. **When / where.** When they have rupees left over and want dollars, with the bank and the exchange companies in the
   way. [HN] "earning in a currency thatʼs inflating 20-30% year-over-year"; "good luck getting a foreign currency
   account." [AAJ] dollars "not being readily available in the open market". [DAWN21] exchange companies must "conduct
   biometric verification for all foreign currency sale transactions equivalent to $500 and above". [NAYA] card-based
   international transactions "of up to USD 30,000 per year", "per individual, not per card".
   → `context.circumstance`. Author's choice: the occasion "payday", the window {3, MONTHS}, Frequency 2 to 3 months out
   of 3, and Prevalence `p_60_80` ("Most"): no public figure says how often.

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** [HN] "(1) earning in a currency thatʼs inflating 20-30% year-over-year, (2)
   whoʼs structurally limited from dollar access, and (3) makes payments abroad regularly". → `context.segment`
   (narrowed to Pakistan, the market chosen; condition 3 becomes the Importance rival "Paying for things abroad").

5. **Who pays.** The saver, alone. [HN] "We currently take a 1% transaction fee". → `persona.decision_maker:
   same_person`, Buyer and payer "Nobody else". Author's choice: no other role is named.

6. **Mechanism.** [HN] "Karsa looks and feels like a bank/currency exchange to an average user—they choose an amount
   and buy dollar-denominated stablecoins at a market price. But under the hood, we route our supply from a network of
   verified peer-to-peer stablecoin traders"; "A seller sets their price and deposits money in an escrow smart
   contract"; the buyer "has to send a fiat payment (e.g., bank transfer, payment app, etc.) to the sellerʼs local
   account + upload a photo for verification"; "we ... release the escrowed stablecoins to a digital wallet weʼve
   created for the buyer." → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, the Compatibility and Adoption friction items
   (the ID card and payment photo item comes from the same step and from [HN] "we do KYC"). Commitment's step "buy a
   small first amount of dollars" is the author's.

7. **Price.** [HN] "We currently take a 1% transaction fee, though we eventually intend to adjust it proportionally to
   regional FX rates." → `commercial.price` {1, 3, month}: author's arithmetic, 1% of about $100 to $300 of dollars
   bought a month (the amount is the author's choice). Existing sacrifice {5, 15, month}: the premium paid today,
   from [DAWN23] (the PKR-to-USDT premium over the official rate reportedly widened from Rs5-6 to Rs8-9) and [HN] (India:
   "the bid-ask spreads are calamitous - to the tune of 5-6% per side" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42885086),
   taken as 3% to 5% of the same $100 to $300 (author's arithmetic). Ability to pay is derived by code (7% to 60%).

8. **Occasions.** [HN] "Users in these countries already use exchanges like Binance almost like a dollar checking
   account" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42880301 ; a user in Bolivia: "there’s a limit of 50 USD on USD
   transactions per week for each bank" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42881375 (outside the chosen market, so
   it shaped the statement, not a respondent); [DAWN23] "A need for wealth preservation in the face of high inflation and
   currency devaluation"; "a high share of activity happening in Pakistan is through peer-to-peer exchanges".

- Rubina Gill → [HN] post, "earning in a currency thatʼs inflating 20-30% year-over-year" and "good luck getting a foreign currency account"; her pay and amount are the author's.
- Zainab Changezi → author's invention, filling a gap: a household decision (Buyer and payer "had to agree") and a dealer found through family, after the grey-market dealers of https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42884769
- Asad Khattak → "this business idea isn’t to just leave a buyer holding the bag" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42883197 ; the partial release is the author's detail.
- Ghulam Sarwar Bhatti → [HN] the founder's relative in Pakistan for whom stablecoins "immediately clicked" once explained; a relative abroad does it for him (the Current-solution escape). His name and details are the author's.
- Sadia Awan → author's invention, filling a gap: a chipped (rather_not_say) story; money is private.
- Waqas Mirza → author's invention, filling a gap: a vague, habitual story with no one occasion (GUESSED).
- Nasreen Bibi → gate No: nothing left over to save, after "They need food and water" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42884419
- Tariq Lodhi → gate No: saves in gold, not dollars, after "why not gold?" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42882904 ; author's invention beyond that.
- Saima Butt → author's invention, filling a gap: gate No, saves through a rotating savings committee in rupees.
- Junaid Malik → gate No: already paid in dollars and keeps them there, after [DAWN23] on freelancers paid in USDT.
- Areeba Soomro → author's invention, filling a gap: gate No, a student with no savings in the window.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- Market: the loader knows no PK currency, so the entry is US / en-US with dollars while the segment and every
  respondent are in Pakistan. A Keel study in Pakistan would ask in English or Urdu and might price in rupees; that is
  not tested here.
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds (most had it, most say getting
  savings into dollars is one of their two, today's ways fall short); the solution splits on paying a seller they have
  never met (eight of thirteen would); the commercial side splits on what the problem costs them today (several pay
  little or nothing besides inflation) and on taking a first step, while the 1% fee itself holds. This is the author's
  reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- Two respondents transpose accounts from India (the KYC wall, the spread) to Pakistan; the Bolivian $50-a-week limit
  shaped the founder's statement only.
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are three months' worth.
- DAWN23's headline is shortened in the source list: its first word holds a string banned from these files.
- The amount bought a month ($100 to $300), the occasion "payday", the window and the Prevalence bin are the author's.

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers mention bills, so I recognise the group and its name is plain, but Farhan's first point is keeping what's left safe after being cheated by a seller, which sits oddly under bills and flat money.
whys.g2: There is no junk answer on this line; both answers are genuine replies to the question.

founder.order_why: It moves sensibly from where I sell, to who and when it applies, to the problem and how savers cope today, then to how the interviews go out, though the 'Sent' label on screens 15 and 16 appears before I have chosen how savers answer or who gets a link.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same heading and question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies'), with the recency question between them.
founder.missing: The flow never asks what I would most want to test: Karsa's mechanism (paying a verified peer-to-peer seller by bank transfer, with stablecoins held in escrow until payment is confirmed) and the 1% fee. It also has no way to choose Pakistan, rupees or Urdu, so the study is marked US although every saver is in Pakistan. It never asks who decides and pays either, which matters where savings are a household decision.

PRIMARY.order_why: It goes sensibly from whether I have a foreign currency account, to whether and how often I had rupees to convert, to what I'd want easier, how buying dollars went, and what keeps it working.
PRIMARY.missing: How much the dollar premium or rate cost me compared with the official rate, and how I felt about the hassle and risk of per-transaction chats and finding dollars actually available.

screens.why2: The question is short and I can answer it on first reading without any unfamiliar word.
screens.why3: It is my own company, so the name is something I already know.
screens.why4: The screen shows only a box to type in, with no options, rows or chips.
screens.why5: The screen keeps my typed name and line exactly as I wrote them, with nothing altered.

screens.why1: Right after naming the project, it makes sense to ask where I start, because that decides who gets asked and in what currency.
screens.why2: "Where will you sell this first?" is plain to me, and I can answer it at once.
screens.why3: I know my first market: Pakistan, where my co-founder's family and our first sellers are.
screens.why4: The value box holds US, but my true answer is Pakistan, and my material says the market table behind this does not know PK, so the true answer appears to be missing.
